name: Liquid cooling
summary: AI racks pack so much power into a small space that fans and cold air can no longer carry the heat away, so water-based cooling is piped right up to the chips.

D1.guide: Which cools a hot pan faster: blowing on it, or running it under water?
text: AI chips get very hot, and they are squeezed close together.
Blowing air over them is like blowing on hot soup. It works for a little heat, but not for a lot.
So builders run cool water through metal plates that touch the chips, and the water carries the heat away.
D1.analogy: Cooling a hot pan under the tap instead of blowing on it.

text: Nearly all the electricity a chip uses becomes heat. Air cooling pushes cold air through the rack with fans, but air holds little heat, so very dense racks would need more airflow than is practical.

Water carries heat far better than air. In **direct-to-chip** cooling, a liquid flows through a **cold plate** pressed onto each processor, then out to a heat exchanger. In **immersion** cooling, whole servers sit in a non-conductive fluid.

The newest AI systems are designed as liquid-cooled racks from the start, so a building that can only do air cooling may not be able to host them. Most liquid-cooled racks still use some air for parts such as power supplies.

columns.title: Air cooling
points: Fans push cold air through the rack
Air holds little heat, so needs lots of airflow

columns.title: Liquid cooling
points: Liquid flows through plates on the chips
Carries far more heat for its volume
Allows denser racks in less floor space
Needs pipes, pumps and leak-safe plumbing

D2.analogy: Cooling a hot pan under the tap instead of blowing on it.
D2.analogyBreaks: Tap water runs once and goes down the drain. Data-centre loops are usually closed: the same liquid circulates, and the heat still has to be dumped somewhere outside, by cooling towers or dry coolers, which may use water of their own.

predict.question: Why did the newest AI racks move from air to liquid cooling?
options: Liquid cooling makes the chips compute faster
So much power is packed into each rack that air cannot carry the heat away fast enough
Fans are too noisy for data centres
Air cooling uses more electricity than the chips
predict.explanation: Packing more chips into one rack concentrates heat. Liquid carries much more heat than the same volume of air, so it can keep up where fans cannot.

text: Open questions: how to retrofit older air-cooled buildings, which liquid approach (cold plates or immersion) wins at even higher densities, and how to reuse the waste heat rather than dumping it.
Liquid cooling can cut cooling energy, but the water story is subtle: closed loops use little, while the outdoor heat rejection can use a lot, depending on climate and design.
